title: The Night Lumi Came
summary: Lumi does not tell stories: she takes you places. A forest, a river of stepping stones, and a white horse to get home.

scenes.text:
Nico was not sleepy. He had put on his pyjamas, he had brushed his teeth, and there he still was, staring at the ceiling. Outside, the city was making its usual noises: a car, another car, a motorbike far away.

Then something very small landed on the window. It was a firefly the size of a grape, with a warm golden belly.

"My name is Lumi," she said. "I don't tell stories. I take you places."

And to say hello, she opened her wings.

Nico never worked out how it happened. One blink, and he was not in his room any more: he was standing on dry leaves, and the trees were so tall you could not see where they ended.

"First stop," said Lumi, and her light grew a little bigger. "Here you don't look. Here you listen."

Nico stood very still. High above, through the topmost branches, came the wind.

They walked until the ground turned soft and cold. Ahead of them, cutting straight across the path, ran a river.

In the middle of the water sat flat stones, one after another, like the buttons on a shirt.

"You cross it hopping," said Lumi. "Stone to stone, no running."

Nico took a breath, aimed at the first one, and made the jump.

On the other side the grass came up to his knees and smelled of freshly cut green.

Something hopped close to his feet and went perfectly still, watching him with two round and very serious eyes: it was a frog.

Further off, circling a yellow flower and paying attention to nobody, a bee was busy working.

"It's getting late," said Lumi. "But walking back would be terribly boring."

Out of the tall grass stepped a white horse, so calm that it looked as though it had been waiting for them for a while.

Nico climbed up, took a good hold of the mane, and then began the gallop.

The horse left them right under the window and trotted away without making a sound.

Up there, on the highest branch, somebody was watching them without blinking even once: an owl.

"See you tomorrow," said Lumi, and her light faded slowly, like a good candle.

Nico climbed into bed. Now he was sleepy.
